title: Our Lady of the Snows (5 August)
hookLine: Rome's great basilica of Mary, founded, legend says, after summer snow

cards: Rome in August. The stones hold the heat long after dark. Shutters are closed against the sun.
And on one hilltop, the story goes, one summer morning, the ground is white. Snow. Not a dusting on a far-off mountain, but snow on a hill in the middle of Rome, in the full heat of summer.
People come out to stare at it. Someone takes it as a message. Today, a church that tradition says was drawn in the snow.

teach.h: A DREAM, AND SNOW ON A HILL.
teach.b: Here's the legend. A Roman husband and wife have no children and want to give what they own to Mary. They pray to know how.
In a dream, she tells them to build a church where snow will fall. The same night, the story says, the pope has the same dream.
In the morning, snow covers part of the Esquiline hill, and the pope traces the outline of the church in it.

teach.h: THE BASILICA OF SAINT MARY MAJOR.
teach.b: That church is the great basilica of Saint Mary Major. So today has two names. In the Church's calendar it's the dedication of that basilica.
In older and popular devotion, it's Our Lady of the Snows.

teach.h: A LEGEND, AND A REAL CHURCH.
teach.b: The snow is told as legend, and the feast keeps the dedication of a real building, still standing, still a place of prayer. Why keep a legend at all? Because of what it points at.
Snow in August is a surprise no one could plan. The psalms speak of God as the one behind the weather. In the Douay-Rheims: "Who giveth snow like wool."
The legend takes that line and puts it on a Roman hill: grace can come out of season, when everything around says it's impossible.
At the basilica, a custom remembers the story on the feast, with white petals let fall from the ceiling during the Mass, like snow. A summer snowfall, made of flowers.

how: Catholics may keep the optional memorial of the Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major on 5 August, known in popular devotion as Our Lady of the Snows.

practice: Look back over the last week for something you didn't expect: a kind word from someone usually short with you, a good day in a hard month, a small thing that went right.
Hold it the way people held the snow that morning, something to look at before you explain it away. If you pray, thank God for it; if you don't, let yourself be surprised by it again.

wordCard.voice: Mary Major, the great Roman basilica behind today's other name, Our Lady of the Snows, recalling the legend of snow on a summer hill.
